subject.title: Codex app-server emits notification:turn/started then goes silent; embedded run wedges for the full stuck-session recovery window

question: Should recovery prioritize preserving an uncertain active native turn, or enforce a bounded abort that releases the channel lane and sends a visible retryable outcome when runtime liveness cannot be proven?
rationale: The code path spans generic session recovery, multiple embedded runtimes, and user-facing delivery semantics; choosing timeout thresholds and the post-abort message/retry contract is a product and reliability policy decision rather than a mechanical one-file fix.

options.title: Adopt a unified bounded-recovery contract
options.body: Define runtime-neutral liveness evidence, abort-to-release cleanup, and an originating-channel retryable failure message, with Codex-specific adapters only where needed.

options.title: Preserve active turns longer
options.body: Require stronger native-runtime evidence before aborting, accepting longer lane blocking while resumed or slow turns remain ambiguous.

options.title: Split only the confirmed sub-bugs
options.body: Land narrow fixes for resumed-turn adoption and recovery cleanup while leaving the broader channel-visible retry contract to a later design item.

recommendation.title: Adopt a unified bounded-recovery contract
recommendation.body: Define runtime-neutral liveness evidence, abort-to-release cleanup, and an originating-channel retryable failure message, with Codex-specific adapters only where needed.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned owner of the closest open diagnostic-recovery issue and the decision crosses the generic terminal-outcome boundary.
